builder_report.summary: V03 part B is complete and all four acceptance criteria pass. The unified router now has three tiers, each with its own entry point (Dopri5::solve, Rodas5p::solve, SwitchingSolver::solve); Tier2/3/4 are removed. Every executed leg is labelled with the driver id from that leg's own run record. Routing uses declared facts through MethodRegistry (new option `regime`), plus a charged n+1-call stiffness screen for small problems that declare nothing. The logarithmic norm is gone and the router's workspace is O(n). A stopped run returns its accepted prefix, the work of every leg and of the preflight, and a typed stop (UnifiedStop). Legs share Options::max_steps, and a fatal callback is not retried. In registry.rs, WindowDriver::run returns a typed error and BatchOutcome keeps the driver's stop. Evidence: 20 base-API tests failed on the base sources by assertion and pass now; 36 contract tests pass; facade suite 533 passed, 0 failed; golden oracle unchanged; SwitchingSolver and ProductionSolver records are byte-identical to base (77/77 digests). Four label assertions in the existing unified test and two example comments were edited. The loop checker exits 1 on a path this task allows. No timing was run.

open_issues: Behaviour of Auto changed: a problem with a supplied Jacobian/JVP/band and no declared regime now runs RODAS5P (base sent it to DOPRI5 when mu2 <= 0); DOPRI5 needs regime(Nonstiff). The explicit trial of an undeclared small problem is limited to min(1000, max_steps/2) attempts (base: all of max_steps); longer non-stiff runs finish on RODAS5P with a finite-difference Jacobian. The values 1000, the dimension limit 10 (kept from base) and the criterion L*span > 3.3*B are design choices, not measured.

VigilodeSolution::status is not exact in one case: a switching stop whose last segment is DOPRI5 and that is neither a callback failure nor the attempt budget is reported as StepSizeTooSmall, because the adapter records no DOPRI5 stop reason. UnifiedStop::is_exact flags it; removing it needs a change to switching.rs (protected).

The stiffness screen sees t0 only: stiffness that develops later (Robertson) is left to the trial budget and fallback, and a fast-oscillating or strongly non-normal non-stiff problem can be sent to RODAS5P.
Finite-difference Jacobians are used without a separate permission (as Rodas5p::solve does), and the switching adapter is still given AllowFiniteDifference; no permission option was added.

Two paths are implemented without a test because the public API cannot reach them with the present routing: UnifiedStop::Refused (fallback leg refuses after a prefix), and a refusal by both entry points after the screen ran (returns Err, screen calls not reported).

Still stored and read by nothing (documented as such, kept because the existing test, example and prelude use them): VigilodeOptions::profile, max_krylov_dim, max_krylov_restarts, invariant_drift_tol; SolverStrategy::HighPerformance routes exactly as Auto; VigilodeWorkspace::step_into is a Heun step no solver calls.

registry.rs items of COD-06 not changed: work_units omits factorizations (changing it would change SwitchingSolver decisions), PexprbWindowDriver treats recoverable callback errors as fatal and records SwitchingMethod::Rodas5p, SolverState/next_solver_state have no caller. BatchStop::Completed still covers minimum-step stops because switching.rs matches the enum exhaustively; the typed stop is in the new field BatchOutcome::failure.
Parts 2 and 3 of the contract tests (16 tests of new API) were written after the implementation; their red state is a compile failure against a scratch copy of the base, not a runtime failure.
The header and the contract_2 comments of the existing unified_production_solver_contracts.rs still use the old vocabulary (multi-tier, VG-1); they are not assertions and were left alone.
Routing through MethodRegistry builds the method catalog several times per solve; the cost was not timed.
A hook flagged rm -rf of a scratch directory as destructive; it was not run. A scratch copy of the base sources remains in the session scratch directory.
rulings: Loop checker: the programme allowlist (MUTATION_GATES.json) does not contain the 12 code paths this task allows, so check_checkpoint.py exits 1 on the first of them. The orchestrator has to extend the allowlist at merge.

Owner decision wanted on the Auto routing constants (explicit trial limit 1000 attempts, dimension limit 10, screen criterion 3.3*B) and on the rule that a supplied derivative runs RODAS5P unless regime(Nonstiff) is declared.

Owner decision wanted on whether to remove the unread options and SolverStrategy::HighPerformance (kept for the existing test, example and prelude), and whether the unified router needs a finite-difference permission like GeneralOdePolicy.
Making status exact for every switching stop, and giving BatchStop a value for minimum-step stops, both require editing the protected switching.rs.

findings.claim: The stiffness screen is described as one-sided (PREDECLARED design_choices.stiffness_screen.one_sided: 'can only move a problem from the explicit trial to RODAS5P'; unified/mod.rs; REPORT_KO.md 3.2). It has a third outcome: a fatal callback at a perturbed probe state y0 + delta e_j ends the solve. This is a regression of VigilODE::solve(Auto) that the report does not list among the behaviour changes.
findings.evidence: Probe rb_guarded_rhs_off_trajectory_probe (review-scratch/review_probe_base_api.rs): y' = -y, y0 = 1, right-hand side fatal for y > 1. Base copy: unified Auto succeeds through DOPRI5 (50 entries, 0 fatal). HEAD: Ok with status callback-failed at t = 0, 2 entries, no leg. Direct Dopri5::solve succeeds on both (49 entries). Records: review-scratch/probe_base_records.json, probe_head_records.json. Code: analyzer.rs stiffness_screen returns the failure for any fatal error, router.rs:70 then returns without a leg. A recoverable error only skips the screen.
findings.correction: State the third outcome in the module documentation and in REPORT_KO.md sections 3.2 and 9.1. Whether a fatal error at a state the trajectory never visits should instead count as 'the screen shows nothing' is an owner decision (the finite-difference Jacobian of Rodas5p::solve already fails on the same right-hand side).
